reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend with a holidays parameter and adds shared predicates (isDailyWeekendSkipping, isWeekendOrHoliday) in shared/schedules.ts that every path calls; parseRecurDate carries frequency/holidays into the schedule data.

duplication.why: The per-occurrence decision 'daily+weekend handling: drop weekend/holiday days, else if skipWeekend move them' is written out separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and twice in schedule-template's createScheduleList, each with its own scan limit.

placement.why: Weekend/holiday predicates and the move logic live in shared/schedules.ts and the handler in server/schedules/app.ts, as the tree does; the occurrence-to-final-day dispatch should also have been a shared function rather than living in each handler.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps; the schedule-template rework is needed to keep budget templates consistent with the new daily rule.

maintainability.why: Shared predicates are good, but the skip-or-move dispatch and ad-hoc scan bounds (MAX_WEEKEND_SCAN, count*7+1000, holiday-based padding) are spread across call sites, so the next weekend rule change has to touch four places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) and createScheduleList (budget/schedule-template.ts) each re-decide skip-vs-move around getDateWithSkippedWeekend instead of one shared occurrence-adjustment function; schedule-template passes noSkipWeekend=!skipsWeekendDays and then re-applies the move itself.

disguised_duplication.where: The same skip-daily/move-otherwise branch reappears reshaped as a firstWeekdayOccurrence path in getNextDate, an if/else push loop in getUpcomingDates, a continue/else-if loop in getDatesInRange and a `skipWeekend && !skipsWeekendDays` ternary twice in schedule-template.ts.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains daily-skip branches for both the forward and reverse lookups plus a holiday pass-through; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template's createScheduleList each carry their own skip-vs-move dispatch.
